dropped.finding: The new arming source compares the runtime store base against a hardcoded Python literal `_CANONICAL_GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT = /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`, but the mount path is a configurable Terraform variable (`gate_scratch_mount`, an overridable `default`). If an operator overrides `gate_scratch_mount`, user_data.sh mounts/marks the volume at the custom path while the Python guard still tests the default literal, so the new post-launch-attach refusal silently fails to arm on the custom path — reverting to the exact marker-only silent-fallback state this change was meant to close.
scenarios: An operator sets a non-default `gate_scratch_mount` (e.g. a different data root); the EBS volume is attached post-launch so user_data.sh's first-boot marker writes never ran; the new configured-path guard compares against the wrong literal and admits gates on root scratch.
